STANDARD.name: Standard walking
STANDARD.desc: The shortest walking route on paths and streets.

WHEELCHAIR.name: Wheelchair or wheeled aid
WHEELCHAIR.desc: Leaves out mapped stairs, raised kerbs and narrow paths, and avoids steep and rough sections.

VISUALLY_IMPAIRED.name: Blind or low vision
VISUALLY_IMPAIRED.desc: Prefers separate footpaths and crossings with signals, and gives detailed steps.

REDUCED_MOBILITY.name: Reduced mobility
REDUCED_MOBILITY.desc: Leaves out stairs, avoids steep slopes and prefers shorter routes with benches.

CUSTOM.name: My own settings
CUSTOM.desc: Start with no restrictions and choose each need yourself.

help.title: Help and privacy
help.howBody: Routes use the walking network from OpenStreetMap. Your requirements, like leaving out stairs, remove paths from the network. Your preferences make some paths more or less favoured. Reports that a moderator has checked are also taken into account.
help.unknownBody: Many paths in the map data have no details about kerbs, surface or width. A missing detail does not mean a path is accessible. We never leave a path out just because details are missing, but we always tell you what is not mapped so you can decide.
help.estimatedBody: Where slopes are not measured, we estimate them from satellite elevation data. Estimates can be wrong near buildings, bridges and underpasses, so they only make a route less favoured. They never leave a path out.
help.safetyBody: This app cannot see traffic, signals, weather or new obstacles. Your location from GPS can be tens of metres off. Always check crossings yourself.
help.privacyBody: You do not need an account. Your settings stay on this device. Your location is only used when you ask for it, is sent to our server only to calculate a route, and is not stored. Searches are answered by our own server, not by third parties. The map background is loaded from the configured map tile server, which receives your IP address and the area you view.
help.keyboardBody: Use Tab to move between controls. In the place search, use the up and down arrow keys and Enter. When the map has focus, the arrow keys move it, plus and minus zoom, and Enter chooses the centre point while you are choosing a point on the map.
help.accessibilityBody: We aim to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA. Automated checks run on every change, but they cannot replace testing by disabled people. If something does not work for you, please report it to the people who run this service.
